description: Table 3 is a single rendered data table (no plots, micrographs or images) titled "Calculated universal anisotropic index (A^U), anisotropy (A_B and A_G) and shear anisotropic factors (A_1, A_2, A_3) of Fe–Mn–Al alloys". It has five columns — "Species", "A^U", "A_B", "A_G" and the merged header "A_1 = A_2 = A_3" — and nine data rows listing body-centred-cubic-derived Fe–Mn–Al compounds: FeAl, Fe0.875Mn0.125Al, Fe0.75Mn0.25Al, Fe0.625Mn0.375Al, Fe0.5Mn0.5Al, Fe0.375Mn0.625Al, Fe0.25Mn0.75Al, Fe0.125Mn0.875Al and MnAl. All values are dimensionless. The A_B column is exactly 0 for every species, reflecting identical Voigt and Reuss bulk moduli. A^U rises from 0.56 for FeAl through 1.03, 1.58, 1.89 to a maximum of 2.06 at Fe0.5Mn0.5Al, then falls to 1.73, 1.36 and 1.84 before jumping to 3.80 for MnAl. A_G tracks the same trend (0.053 → 0.171 → 0.276), and the shear anisotropic factors A_1 = A_2 = A_3 mirror it as well (1.96 → 3.46 → 4.97). The table therefore demonstrates that FeAl is the most elastically isotropic compound in the Fe1−xMnxAl series, that Fe0.5Mn0.5Al has the largest anisotropy among the Fe-containing alloys, and that MnAl is by far the most anisotropic of all.

subfigures.description: A single tabular figure with columns Species, A^U, A_B, A_G and A_1 = A_2 = A_3, containing nine rows for FeAl to MnAl. A_B is 0 in every row; A^U peaks at 2.06 for Fe0.5Mn0.5Al and reaches 3.80 for MnAl; A_G ranges 0.053–0.276; A_1 = A_2 = A_3 ranges 1.96–4.97.

observations.observation: Table 3 reports four anisotropy quantities per species: A^U (universal anisotropic index), A_B, A_G and the shear anisotropic factor A_1 = A_2 = A_3.
The table contains nine rows: FeAl, Fe0.875Mn0.125Al, Fe0.75Mn0.25Al, Fe0.625Mn0.375Al, Fe0.5Mn0.5Al, Fe0.375Mn0.625Al, Fe0.25Mn0.75Al, Fe0.125Mn0.875Al and MnAl.
A_B is printed as 0 for every one of the nine species.
FeAl has the smallest values in the table for A^U (0.56), A_G (0.053) and A_1 = A_2 = A_3 (1.96).
MnAl has the largest values in the table, with A^U = 3.80, A_G = 0.276 and A_1 = A_2 = A_3 = 4.97.
A^U increases monotonically with Mn content from FeAl (0.56) to Fe0.5Mn0.5Al (2.06), then decreases to 1.36 at Fe0.25Mn0.75Al before rising again to 1.84 at Fe0.125Mn0.875Al.
Among the Fe-containing compounds the maximum A^U is 2.06 at Fe0.5Mn0.5Al and the maximum A_1 = A_2 = A_3 is 3.46, also at Fe0.5Mn0.5Al.
The citing text states that the A_B value is zero for all alloys because the bulk moduli are the same by the Voigt or Reuss methods.

The citing text states that the descending order of anisotropy for the Fe–Mn–Al alloys is MnAl > Fe0.5Mn0.5Al > Fe0.625Mn0.375Al > Fe0.125Mn0.875Al > Fe0.375Mn0.625Al > Fe0.75Mn0.25Al > Fe0.25Mn0.75Al > Fe0.875Mn0.125Al > FeAl.
The citing text states that A_1, A_2 and A_3 represent the anisotropies of the shear modulus in the (100), (010) and (001) planes respectively.
The citing text states that the changes in A_G and A^U follow the same trend as shown in Fig. 8.
The citing text states that a low A_G value for all alloys shows weak anisotropy in the shear modulus.

measured_quantities: shear anisotropic factors A_1 = A_2 = A_3 (dimensionless)
